items.rationale: The authority declares clock domains with injected bounded sources and kinds (§4.2), directed source→destination mappings with tolerance (§4.3), checked signed arithmetic for overflow, monotonic regression detection, full-range unsigned distance, and single-mutex synchronization (§4.4). UnknownClock, ClockSourceFailure, ClockOutOfBounds, ClockRegression, ClockOverflow, MissingMapping, and ToleranceExceeded are distinct deterministic outcomes.

items.rationale: The permit is immutable with construction-time validation of every bound field (§5.2); PermitId is the FNV-1a digest over all bound fields including the nonce, so a changed nonce yields a different identity (§5.3). Consume compares the SessionContext field-by-field before the atomic try_consume (§7.3 step 1-2); replay scope is explicitly controller-scoped (D-4, §6.1).

items.rationale: Handles bind ManagerScope, ControllerId, Generation, and SessionId (§7.1); the manager never derives identity from a per-manager counter, and re-registration supersedes the prior identity in a bounded window. The outcome table (§7.2) rejects stale (StaleHandle), foreign (ForeignHandle), recreated-controller (RecreatedController), and forged (InvalidHandle) handles without addressing a live session.

items.rationale: The transition table (§7.4) defines every legal predecessor→successor pair for declared→armed→active→closing→closed plus Expire/Revoke/MarkEvidenceIncomplete terminal transitions; the idempotency table enumerates the safe AlreadyApplied repeats; terminal lockout (TerminalState) and invalid transitions (InvalidTransition) are exhaustive via a constexpr static table.

items.rationale: Shared mutable state is guarded by per-component std::mutex (§9.1); try_consume is a single atomic check-then-insert critical section so N concurrent consumptions of one permit yield exactly one Ok and N−1 failures (§6.2); the manager serializes all consumes and transitions under one lock, and TimeAuthority/PermitRegistry/SessionManager are non-copyable/non-movable.
